lines.trans: Just the broadcasts and events I canceled for today and tomorrow come to ten.
Still, you have to go to the corporate event the day after tomorrow—the penalty fee is steep.
The doctor said she must stay hospitalized at least four days for all her tests, right?
Yes, a minimum of four days.
CEO Byun, my name is Tak Ye-jin—in a way I am the main culprit behind this accident...
Would you mind staying out of this—and keeping your mouth shut too?
Byun Entertainment is a major agency—will the company go under if Cindy rests for a few days?
When there is a doctor's diagnosis, ignoring a patient's free will to force her to work is unlawful as far as I know.
And threatening financial losses borders on criminal intimidation too—that is illegal, right?
Yeah, that is what I heard too!

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?
Did you hear about this tomorrow?
I was busy today because of tomorrow.
I want to got caught right now.
How about trying to got caught together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 오늘 내일 잡힌 방송이랑 행사 취소한 것만 열 건이야.
examples.trans: Just the broadcasts and events I canceled for today and tomorrow come to ten.
Here the word for 'events' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 오늘 내일 잡힌 방송이랑 행사 취소한 것만 열 건이야.
examples.trans: Just the broadcasts and events I canceled for today and tomorrow come to ten.
This expression comes from 'canceled'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Native Korean numeral used with hours (시), age (살), and general counters.

examples.trans: It is ten o'clock now.
Please give me ten apples.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 오늘 내일 잡힌 방송이랑 행사 취소한 것만 열 건이야.
examples.trans: Just the broadcasts and events I canceled for today and tomorrow come to ten.
Here the word for 'are ten cases' is key.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 근데 내일모레 기업 행사는 가야 돼, 위약금도 세.
examples.trans: Still, you have to go to the corporate event the day after tomorrow—the penalty fee is steep.
Here the word for 'the day after tomorrow' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 근데 내일모레 기업 행사는 가야 돼, 위약금도 세.
examples.trans: Still, you have to go to the corporate event the day after tomorrow—the penalty fee is steep.
Here the word for 'corporate' is key.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 근데 내일모레 기업 행사는 가야 돼, 위약금도 세.
examples.trans: Still, you have to go to the corporate event the day after tomorrow—the penalty fee is steep.
Here the word for 'breach-of-contract penalty too' is key.
It really is strongly, boldly compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is strongly, boldly and nice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나흘은 입원해야 한다고 검사할 것도 많고, 그렇지?
examples.trans: The doctor said she must stay hospitalized at least four days for all her tests, right?
Here the word for 'four days at least' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나흘은 입원해야 한다고 검사할 것도 많고, 그렇지?
examples.trans: The doctor said she must stay hospitalized at least four days for all her tests, right?
This expression comes from 'must be hospitalized'.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나흘은 입원해야 한다고 검사할 것도 많고, 그렇지?
examples.trans: The doctor said she must stay hospitalized at least four days for all her tests, right?
This expression comes from 'to examine'.

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, or abundant
meanings.note: Used for both countable and uncountable nouns.

examples.trans: Because it's the weekend, there are many people at the department store.

examples.text: 오늘 해야 할 일이 너무 많다.
examples.trans: There is too much work to do today.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.
Did you hear about this at least?
I was busy today because of at least.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used before time nouns like 이번 주 (this week)

examples.trans: There is a meeting this Friday.
I will definitely succeed this time.

meanings.note: Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 변 대표님, 저 탁예진이라고 합니다, 이번 사고의 주범인데...
examples.trans: CEO Byun, my name is Tak Ye-jin—in a way I am the main culprit behind this accident...
Here the word for 'am the main culprit...' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 야, 근데 거기 내가 왜 끼냐고?
examples.trans: Hey, why on earth would I get dragged into that?
This expression comes from 'get roped in?'.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.

meanings.note: noun mouth

examples.trans: Open mouth.
Mouth hurts.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 끼지 말아 줄래요? 입도 좀 다물어줬으면 하고.
examples.trans: Would you mind staying out of this—and keeping your mouth shut too?
This expression comes from 'if you shut it'.
It really is is loud, so compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is is loud, so and nice.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.
Did you hear about this a few days?
I was busy today because of a few days.

examples.text: 말을 잘 못 알아들으시네. 신디 이번 주 쉬죠?
examples.trans: You are not catching my meaning. Let's have Cindy rest this week, shall we?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 쉬다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (take a break, rest).

meanings.note: Used for room doors, building entrances, and car doors

examples.trans: It's cold, so please close the door.

examples.text: 차 문을 열 때 옆 차를 조심하세요.
examples.trans: Watch out for the next car when opening your car door.

examples.text: 병원 문 닫고 네 매형 백수 되게 생겼다니까.
examples.trans: The clinic is about to close and turn your brother-in-law into an unemployed man.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 닫다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (close and).

meanings.note: ends in the Sino-Korean suffix -사 ('specialist/professional')

examples.trans: My younger sibling is a doctor working at a hospital.
If you have a high fever, see a doctor.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 의사의 진단이 있는데 환자의 자유 의지를 무시하고 일을 강요하시는 거 안 된다고 알고 있는데.
examples.trans: When there is a doctor's diagnosis, ignoring a patient's free will to force her to work is unlawful as far as I know.
Here the word for 'diagnosis' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 신디가 월등히 많이 다쳐서 그렇지 나도 충분히 다쳤거든, 나도 환자야!
examples.trans: Only because Cindy got hurt way worse do I look fine—I am plenty injured too, I am a patient!
Here the word for 'am a patient!' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 의사의 진단이 있는데 환자의 자유 의지를 무시하고 일을 강요하시는 거 안 된다고 알고 있는데.
examples.trans: When there is a doctor's diagnosis, ignoring a patient's free will to force her to work is unlawful as far as I know.
Here the word for 'free' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 반대지, 절대 7은 안 나올 테니까 난 돈은 안 따겠다는 의지지!
examples.trans: Quite the opposite—since it will never sink to seven, it shows my resolve not to take your money!
Here the word for 'is my resolve!' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 의사의 진단이 있는데 환자의 자유 의지를 무시하고 일을 강요하시는 거 안 된다고 알고 있는데.
examples.trans: When there is a doctor's diagnosis, ignoring a patient's free will to force her to work is unlawful as far as I know.
This expression comes from 'ignoring and'.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 의사의 진단이 있는데 환자의 자유 의지를 무시하고 일을 강요하시는 거 안 된다고 알고 있는데.
examples.trans: When there is a doctor's diagnosis, ignoring a patient's free will to force her to work is unlawful as far as I know.
This expression comes from 'forcing (honorific)'.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 근데 백승찬, 나 너한테 약간 부끄러우려고 그런다.
examples.trans: Still, Baek Seung-chan, I am starting to feel a little embarrassed in front of you.
Here the word for 'a little' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이게 약간 협박죄랑도 관련이 있는 거고, 안 되지?
examples.trans: And threatening financial losses borders on criminal intimidation too—that is illegal, right?
Here the word for 'with criminal intimidation too' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이게 약간 협박죄랑도 관련이 있는 거고, 안 되지?
examples.trans: And threatening financial losses borders on criminal intimidation too—that is illegal, right?
Here the word for 'connection' is key.

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
